rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: ban on criminal history inquiries before conditional offer
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until after making a conditional offer. The only exceptions are methamphetamine production on federally assisted premises and lifetime sex offender registration. Before accepting any application fee, the provider must disclose in writing whether criminal history is considered and that the applicant may submit evidence of inaccuracies or rehabilitation.
rules.key_value: No criminal record inquiry before conditional offer
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers (landlords, owners, lessors, sublessors, agents) of rental dwelling units in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Providers may consider methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exempt if the premises is owner-occupied and has 4 or fewer units.

rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 for a first violation, up to $5,000 for a second violation within 5 years, and up to $10,000 for two or more prior violations within 7 years. Enforced through Division on Civil Rights complaints; no private court action.

regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is computed from the act's text ('first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment', approved June 18, 2021), which gives January 1, 2022. The document does not state this date explicitly.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: limits on criminal records considered after conditional offer
rules.requirement: Providers may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records, or juvenile adjudications. After a conditional offer, they may consider only specified serious convictions or convictions within lookback periods. A withdrawal requires an individualized assessment, written reasons, and an opportunity to appeal.
rules.key_value: Lookback: 1st degree 6 years; 2nd/3rd degree 4 years; 4th degree 1 year (lifetime for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, etc.)

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: ban on advertisements excluding applicants with criminal records
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not publish advertisements or use application forms stating they will not consider applicants with arrests or convictions, except for the limited methamphetamine and sex-offender-registry exceptions. They also may not disseminate or misuse an applicant's criminal record.

rules.title: Ban on requiring drug or alcohol tests of rental applicants
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not require rental applicants to take a drug or alcohol test. They also may not request consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
